Talulah Jane Riley-Milburn (born 26 September 1985) is an English actress. She has appeared in films, including Pride & Prejudice (2005), St Trinian's (2007) and its sequel St Trinian's 2: The Legend of Fritton's Gold (2009), The Boat That Rocked (2009), and Inception (2010). She has also appeared on the HBO science fiction western series Westworld (2016–2018) and the FX biographical miniseries Pistol (2022).

Early life and education

[edit]

Talulah Jane Riley-Milburn[1][2] was born on 26 September 1985[3] in Hemel Hempstead in Hertfordshire, where she grew up[4] as the only child of Una Riley, founder of a security systems company and a public relations company,[5] and Doug Milburn, formerly head of the National Crime Squad. As of October 2021[update], her father works as a screenwriter[citation needed] and has written episodes of Silent Witness and The Bill. Riley was educated at Cheltenham Ladies' College, independent Berkhamsted Collegiate School, and Haberdashers' Girls' School. While acting in London, she studied for a degree in Natural Sciences at the Open University.[6]

Career

[edit]

Television

[edit]

Riley's television credits include episodes of Poirot (2003), Marple (2006), and Doctor Who (2008's "Silence in the Library" and "Forest of the Dead").[7] She played Lila, a lovestruck writer, in the short-lived E4 series Nearly Famous (2007).[8] She played Angela in the first two seasons of the television series Westworld.[9]

Stage

[edit]

Riley made her stage debut in The Philadelphia Story at the Old Vic in 2005. Her performance in a 2006 revival of Tennessee Williams' Summer and Smoke was described by critic Rachel Read as "delightful".[10]

Film

[edit]

Riley played Mary Bennet in the 2005 version of Pride and Prejudice and Marianne in 2009's The Boat That Rocked. She starred in the 2007 film St Trinian's and its 2009 sequel St Trinian's: The Legend of Fritton's Gold.[11][12]

Riley appeared as a disguise used by Tom Hardy's character in Inception (2010). Also in 2010, Love and Distrust was released direct-to-video, featuring five unique short films, the first of which was The Summer House, in which Riley was co-lead, opposite Robert Pattinson. Available as a standalone download, The Summer House was the number one film on iTunes worldwide on its first day of release, holding that position for several days.[13] She also appeared in White Frog.[14]

Between 2009 and 2015, Riley developed an idea and story by her father into a screenplay, then ultimately directed (after being unable to hire another director to helm the project)[15] and starred in the resulting feature film Scottish Mussel.

Writing

[edit]

Her debut novel, Acts of Love, was published by Hodder & Stoughton in August 2016.[16][17] In June 2022, Riley released her second novel, The Quickening, also published by Hodder & Stoughton. She is also listed as a contributor to Encounters with Jane Austen: Celebrating 250 years.

Other

[edit]

She was featured on the March 2010 cover of Esquire.[18][19] In 2011, she was named a "Brit to Watch" by the British Academy of Film and Television Arts.[20]

Personal life

[edit]

Riley married billionaire Elon Musk in 2010 at Dornoch Cathedral in the Scottish Highlands.[21][22] The couple divorced in March 2012.[23][24]

In July 2013, Musk and Riley remarried.[25] In a 60 Minutes interview in 2014, the couple said they had reconciled and were living together again, along with Musk's five children from his first marriage to Justine Wilson.[26] On 31 December 2014, Musk filed for divorce a second time, but later withdrew the action.[27][28] After living separately for six months, Riley filed for a second divorce in Los Angeles Superior Court on 21 March 2016.[21] The divorce was finalised in October 2016.[29]

Riley married actor Thomas Brodie-Sangster on 22 June 2024 in Hertfordshire.[30]

In July 2013, Musk and Riley remarried.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kimble |first=Lindsay |date=18 November 2016 |title=Elon Musk and Talulah Riley Divorced: Report |url=https://people.com/movies/elon-musk-and-talulah-riley-divorced/ |access-date=13 November 2021 |website=People |language=en |archive-date=8 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908185659/http://people.com/movies/elon-musk-and-talulah-riley-divorced/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In a ''[[60 Minutes]]'' interview in 2014, the couple said they had reconciled and were living together again, along with Musk's five children from his first marriage to Justine Wilson.<ref>{{cite news |first=Scott |last=Pelley |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tesla-and-spacex-elon-musks-industrial-empire |title=Tesla and SpaceX: Elon Musk's industrial empire |publisher=[[CBS News]] |date=30 March 2014 |access-date=30 March 2014 |archive-date=31 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140331065825/http://www.cbsnews.com/news/tesla-and-spacex-elon-musks-industrial-empire/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On 31 December 2014, Musk filed for divorce a second time, but later withdrew the action.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.yahoo.com/apnewsbreak-elon-musk-actress-wife-split-again-005556297.html |title=Elon Musk, actress wife split again |publisher=Yahoo! News |date=31 December 2014 |access-date=2 January 2015 |archive-date=1 January 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150101081837/http://news.yahoo.com/apnewsbreak-elon-musk-actress-wife-split-again-005556297.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cnbc.com/id/102305285 |title=Elon Musk, actress wife split again |date=2 January 2015 |access-date=2 January 2015 |archive-date=2 January 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150102161151/http://www.cnbc.com/id/102305285 |url-status=dead }}</ref> After living separately for six months, Riley filed for a second divorce in [[Los Angeles Superior Court]] on 21 March 2016.<ref name="marriage"/> The divorce was finalised in October 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tv3.ie/xpose/article/entertainment-news/220688/Elon-Musk-and-Talulah-Riley-reach-divorce-settlement |title=Elon Musk and Talulah Riley reach divorce settlement |work=[[TV3 (Ireland)]] |date=21 October 2016 |access-date=22 October 2016 |archive-date=22 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161022215425/http://www.tv3.ie/xpose/article/entertainment-news/220688/Elon-Musk-and-Talulah-Riley-reach-divorce-settlement |url-status=live }}</ref>

Riley married actor [[Thomas Brodie-Sangster]] on 22 June 2024 in [[Hertfordshire]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/thomas-brodie-sangster-talulah-riley-wedding-elon-musk-b2567287.html|title='Love Actually' star Thomas Brodie-Sangster, 34, marries actor Talulah Riley in romantic ceremony|last=Muir|first=Ellie|date=24 June 2024|work=The Independent}}</ref>
